critical_code_review_comments: PromoVideo.jsx useEffect threshold of 100KB is fine, but consider also requiring a content-type that either starts with 'video/' OR equals 'application/octet-stream' for a tighter check. Current accept-anything-except-html/json works but would also accept e.g. text/plain or image/* if the CDN ever mislabels — extremely unlikely, just defensive.
Hero caption text 'Trailer · Tennant Equipment Insights (official YouTube). Drop a Sora 2-rendered /promo.mp4 ...' is now incorrect once hasLocalMp4=true — gate this string on the same flag.
TECH_STACK still lists Video='Sora 2 (this promo was AI-generated)' which is technically a MOCKED integration (ffmpeg slideshow substitute). Acceptable for demo copy but flagged for transparency.

rca of the issue: Original bug: PromoVideo.jsx accepted only Content-Type starting with 'video/'. Production CDN serves /promo.mp4 with 'application/octet-stream' so the strict check failed and the YouTube iframe rendered. Fix in lines 57-71 now treats any non-html/non-json content-type with len > 100KB as a valid video. Preview HEAD returns video/mp4 + 1098557 bytes which passes the new check; the curl-verified production scenario (octet-stream + 1098557) would also pass. No backend changes.
